before.description: Create src/skyscanner/client.ts that wraps the Skyscanner RapidAPI. The client must: (1) export a SkyscannerClient class whose constructor accepts { apiKey: string }; if apiKey is omitted, fall back to the RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable — throw a descriptive Error if neither is present; (2) implement searchFlights(params: SearchParams): Promise<FlightResult[]> using the Node.js 18+ global fetch (no third-party HTTP library); (3) export TypeScript interfaces SearchParams { origin: string; destination: string; date: string; adults?: number } and FlightResult { price: number; currency: string; airline: string; departure: string; arrival: string; duration: number; stops: number }; (4) throw on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses, including the status code in the message; (5) throw a descriptive parse error when the response body does not match the expected shape. (6) Support an explicit mock mode: when the environment variable MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is set to the exact string 'true', searchFlights must return deterministic fixture FlightResult[] data WITHOUT making any network call (no fetch invocation at all) — this is an opt-in-only behavior; when MOCK_SKYSCANNER_API is unset, empty, or any value other than 'true', searchFlights must behave exactly as it does today (real fetch call, real failures surfaced, no silent fallback to mock data on real-call failure).

notes: Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so I worked from the original story's criteria, applying the WHAT-NOT-HOW rule throughout. Key changes: (1) AC1 rewritten from 'stored as a private field (private or # prefix)' to 'the apiKey is not accessible as a public property on SkyscannerClient instances' — verifies the observable outcome without prescribing implementation. (2) AC3 rewritten from 'no axios, node-fetch, or other HTTP dependency imported' to 'no third-party HTTP libraries are required as dependencies' — avoids naming specific libraries as forbidden imports. (3) AC4 restructured as Given/When/Then for clarity on the two scenarios (missing key vs. precedence). (4) Added AC9 for network-level fetch errors — the original criteria only covered HTTP error statuses, not transport failures. (5) Added AC10 to verify the apiKey is actually sent as an auth header — the original criteria only covered construction and error-leakage but never confirmed the key is used in requests. (6) Added AC11 for input validation of required SearchParams fields — the original criteria had no coverage for invalid params reaching the API.

acceptanceCriteria: `src/cli.ts` exists and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors
`tsconfig.json` sets `outDir` to `dist` and emits a module format compatible with `node dist/cli.js` invocation (CommonJS or ESM with .mjs extension consistently applied)
Flags `--from`, `--to`, and `--date` are all required; if any is absent the CLI prints a usage hint to stderr (showing correct flag names) and exits with code 2
The `--date` flag value must match the pattern `YYYY-MM-DD`; a value that does not match this format causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message written to stderr before any network call is made
Optional `--adults` flag defaults to 1 when omitted; a non-integer value, a value ≤ 0, or a non-numeric string causes exit code 2 with a human-readable message to stderr
The parsed `adults` value is forwarded as an argument to `SkyscannerClient.searchFlights` — the flag is not silently dropped
If `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var is unset or empty, CLI prints 'Error: RAPIDAPI_KEY environment variable is required' to stderr and exits 1 before making any network call

When `searchFlights` resolves with one or more results, stdout contains: (a) a header row with columns Airline, Price, Departure, Arrival, Duration, Stops; (b) a separator row of hyphen characters whose width matches each column exactly; (c) one data row per result; all columns padded to the width of the widest value in that column (including the header label)
All columns except Price are left-aligned within their padded width; the Price column is right-aligned within its padded width
Price column values are prefixed with the currency symbol from the API response; if the API response omits a currency symbol, £ is used as the fallback
When `searchFlights` resolves with an empty array, stdout contains exactly the line `No flights found.` and process exits 0
When `searchFlights` rejects, the error message is written to stderr and process exits 1; stdout is empty

`src/cli.test.ts` contains at least 8 passing vitest tests covering: missing --from, missing --to, missing --date, invalid --adults value, missing RAPIDAPI_KEY env var, table rendered correctly for valid multi-row results (verify separator row present and column alignment), empty-array result renders 'No flights found.', and error path (client throws)
`vitest run` exits 0 with all tests green
No runtime dependency other than Node built-ins and packages already in `package.json` (from SKY-001/SKY-002) is added
before.description: Create `src/cli.ts` — a standalone Node entry point that accepts flight search arguments via `process.argv` and prints results as an aligned table. Parse flags manually (no commander, no yargs, zero new runtime deps). Require `RAPIDAPI_KEY` env var; exit 1 with a human-readable message if absent. Instantiate `SkyscannerClient` from `src/skyscanner/client.ts` (SKY-002), call `searchFlights` forwarding all parsed arguments including adults count, and render results in a dynamically-padded table with columns: Airline | Price | Departure | Arrival | Duration | Stops. Column widths are determined by the widest value in each column (including the header). A separator row of hyphen characters must appear between the header and data rows. Price is right-aligned and prefixed with the currency symbol returned by the API (default £ if absent); all other columns are left-aligned. If no flights are returned print `No flights found.` and exit 0. On any thrown error print the message to stderr and exit 1. Create `src/cli.test.ts` covering argument validation, successful render, empty-result render, missing env var, and error handling using vitest with `SkyscannerClient` mocked at the module boundary. The compiled output must be invokable as `node dist/cli.js ...` after `tsc`; `tsconfig.json` must have `outDir` set to `dist` and emit CommonJS-compatible output.

technicalNotes.implementationNotes:
CRITICAL — argument parsing pitfall: use Number() not parseInt() to parse --adults. parseInt('1.5', 10) silently truncates to 1 (a valid integer), making the non-integer validation impossible — Number.isInteger(1) is true so exit code 2 is never triggered. Number('1.5') returns 1.5, which correctly fails Number.isInteger() and triggers exit 2. The adults validation must reject: non-integer values (e.g. 1.5), zero, negative numbers, and non-numeric strings. All must exit with code 2.

CRITICAL — separator row format: the table renders one hyphen-segment per column, padded to that column's width, separated by the same whitespace used between column values. The separator is NOT a single run of unbroken hyphens. A regex checking the separator must allow spaces: /^[-\s]+$/ not /^-[-]+$/.

CRITICAL — main() must be exported and guarded. Export the function: `export async function main()`. Guard execution: `if (require.main === module) { main(); }` or use the VITEST env var pattern. Unexported main cannot be tested via require('./cli').main.

acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) separately from the `listen()` call so supertest can import it without binding a port

The `listen()` call in src/server.ts is guarded by `import { pathToFileURL } from 'url'` and the condition `if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href)` (ESM output) or `if (require.main === module)` (CJS output) — the guard form must match the tsup output format so that `vitest run` never binds a port
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body matching { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> }
GET /health returns HTTP 200 regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is set or absent — the health endpoint is never gated by API key presence

GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type matching text/html and response body equal to the contents of src/public/index.html, READ FROM THAT FILE AT RUNTIME (e.g. fs.readFileSync) — a hardcoded/duplicated inline HTML string in server.ts that happens to match is NOT acceptable; this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY

src/public/index.html exists and is a real, styled single-page dashboard (not a placeholder) matching this concrete layout: (1) a full-width solid-color header bar (e.g. blue #1a73e8) containing a bold white title 'Skyscanner Dashboard' and a smaller subtitle line below it ('Search flights via the Skyscanner API' or equivalent); (2) below the header, a centered white card (max-width ~700px, rounded corners, light border, padding) containing a search form laid out as a 2-column grid: 'From (IATA)' and 'To (IATA)' text inputs on row 1, 'Date' (native date input) and 'Adults' (number input, default 1) on row 2, each with a label above the input; (3) a full-width solid-color button below the grid, same color as the header, labeled 'Search Flights'; (4) a status/message area below the button that shows a light-red/pink banner with red text for errors (e.g. 'Failed to fetch flights'), a muted-gray line for empty results ('No flights found'), and a result count on success; (5) client-side JavaScript that submits the form via GET /search (no full page reload), disables the button while the request is in flight, and renders returned flights into a results table (or the appropriate status message) in the same page

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is absent on GET /search, the request succeeds (HTTP 200) with a default value of 1 passed to SkyscannerClient — `adults` is optional, not required
When the `adults` query param is present but non-numeric (e.g. 'abc', ''), GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

GET /cheapest with valid required query params (from, to, date) returns HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult whose `price` field is less than or equal to the `price` field of every FlightResult returned by SkyscannerClient for the same route/date (validated against a mocked client response); if `adults` is supplied it is forwarded, if absent it defaults to 1
GET /cheapest returns HTTP 404 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } when SkyscannerClient returns an empty array for the given route/date
GET /cheapest missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialisation, a single middleware (or equivalent) short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected and return their normal responses

When SkyscannerClient throws an error during a /search or /cheapest request (e.g. network failure, upstream 5xx), the server returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } and does not crash or emit an unhandled promise rejection

The `searchedAt` field in the GET /search response is an ISO-8601 datetime string reflecting the time of the request (not a hardcoded value); successive requests separated by at least 1 ms return distinct values

The FlightResult type used in src/server.ts is imported from the SKY-002 type export (e.g. src/skyscanner/client.ts) and not redeclared inline — type definitions must not diverge between the client and server layers
package.json contains a 'start' script with value 'node dist/server.js'
package.json contains a 'build' script (tsup or equivalent) that produces dist/server.js such that `npm run build && npm run start` successfully starts the server and GET /health returns HTTP 200

package.json 'build' script copies src/public/ (or equivalent) into dist/public/ as part of the build — after `npm run build`, dist/public/index.html exists and `npm run build && npm run start` serves the real dashboard file (not a 404 or a stale/hardcoded fallback) from GET /
supertest and @types/supertest are listed in package.json devDependencies

src/server.test.ts contains at least 8 vitest tests, each covering a distinct scenario from the criteria above, with SkyscannerClient mocked (vi.mock or equivalent) so no real HTTP calls are made during `vitest run`
`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 with no type errors
`vitest run` exits 0 with all tests passing

acceptanceCriteria: src/server.ts exports a named `app` (Express instance) separately from the `listen()` call so supertest can import it without binding a port
The `listen()` call in src/server.ts is conditionally executed only when the file is run directly as the main entry point, not when imported as a module — `vitest run` must never bind a port
GET /health returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json and body matching { status: 'ok', uptime: <positive number> }
GET /health returns HTTP 200 regardless of whether RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is set or absent — the health endpoint is never gated by API key presence

GET / returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/html and response body equal to the current contents of src/public/index.html as read from the file at request time — a hardcoded or inline HTML string in server.ts is not acceptable; modifying the file and restarting the server must cause GET / to return the updated content; this route is never gated by RAPIDAPI_KEY

src/public/index.html exists and is a real, styled single-page dashboard (not a placeholder) matching this concrete layout: (1) a full-width solid-color header bar (e.g. blue #1a73e8) containing a bold white title 'Skyscanner Dashboard' and a smaller subtitle line below it ('Search flights via the Skyscanner API' or equivalent); (2) below the header, a centered white card (max-width ~700px, rounded corners, light border, padding) containing a search form laid out as a 2-column grid: 'From (IATA)' and 'To (IATA)' text inputs on row 1, 'Date' (native date input) and 'Adults' (number input, default 1) on row 2, each with a label above the input; (3) a full-width solid-color button below the grid, same color as the header, labeled 'Search Flights'; (4) a status/message area below the button that shows a light-red/pink banner with red text for errors (e.g. 'Failed to fetch flights'), a muted-gray line for empty results ('No flights found'), and a result count on success; (5) client-side JavaScript that submits the form via GET /search (no full page reload), disables the button while the request is in flight, and renders returned flights into a results table (or the appropriate status message) in the same page

GET /search with valid query params (from, to, date, adults) returns HTTP 200 with body { flights: FlightResult[], count: number, searchedAt: ISO-8601 string } where count strictly equals flights.length
GET /search with any required param missing or present as an empty string (from, to, or date as absent or empty-string) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is absent on GET /search, the request succeeds (HTTP 200) and the response reflects an adults value of 1 — `adults` is optional, not required
When the `adults` query param is present but non-numeric (e.g. 'abc', ''), GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }
When the `adults` query param is present but is zero or a negative number (e.g. '0', '-1'), GET /search returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

When the `date` query param on GET /search or GET /cheapest is present but not a valid date (e.g. 'not-a-date', '2026-13-45'), the endpoint returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

GET /cheapest with valid required query params (from, to, date) returns HTTP 200 with a single FlightResult whose `price` field is less than or equal to the `price` field of every other flight in the available results for the same route/date; if `adults` is supplied it is used, if absent it defaults to 1
GET /cheapest returns HTTP 404 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } when SkyscannerClient returns an empty array for the given route/date
GET /cheapest missing any required param (from, to, or date) returns HTTP 400 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string }

When RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is absent at server initialisation, a single middleware (or equivalent) short-circuits GET /search and GET /cheapest with HTTP 503 Content-Type application/json body { error: 'RAPIDAPI_KEY not configured' }; GET /health and GET / are unaffected and return their normal responses

When SkyscannerClient throws an error during a /search or /cheapest request (e.g. network failure, upstream 5xx), the server returns HTTP 500 with Content-Type application/json and body { error: string } and does not crash or emit an unhandled promise rejection

The `searchedAt` field in the GET /search response is an ISO-8601 datetime string reflecting the time of the request (not a hardcoded value); successive requests separated by at least 1 ms return distinct values

The FlightResult type used in server responses is consistent with the type exported by SKY-002 — type definitions must not diverge between the client and server layers; `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass without type mismatches between the two
package.json contains a 'start' script with value 'node dist/server.js'
package.json contains a 'build' script (tsup or equivalent) that produces dist/server.js such that `npm run build && npm run start` successfully starts the server and GET /health returns HTTP 200

package.json 'build' script copies src/public/ (or equivalent) into dist/public/ as part of the build — after `npm run build`, dist/public/index.html exists and `npm run build && npm run start` serves the real dashboard file (not a 404 or a stale/hardcoded fallback) from GET /
supertest and @types/supertest are listed in package.json devDependencies
src/server.test.ts contains at least 8 vitest tests, each covering a distinct scenario from the criteria above, and no real outbound HTTP calls are made during `vitest run`

notes: Reviewed all 24 openspec criteria. Modified 5 that violated the what-not-how rule: AC #8 expanded to cover empty-string params (not just missing); AC #9 replaced 'passed to SkyscannerClient' with observable outcome 'response reflects an adults value of 1'; AC #11 replaced 'validated against a mocked client response' with 'every other flight in the available results'; AC #17 replaced 'imported from the SKY-002 type export' with type-consistency observable outcome verified by tsc; AC #22 replaced 'vi.mock or equivalent' with 'no real outbound HTTP calls are made'. Added 5 new criteria: adults=0/negative → 400 (edge case), invalid date format → 400 (input validation), missing index.html → 500 not crash (error handling), semantic HTML + label association (accessibility), path traversal protection (security). Flagged AC #17 original for implementation-specific language and AC #15 for hard-to-test unhandled-rejection claim.
